messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Text: Q: How long does Zoloft (sertraline) withdrawal last? A: Sertraline (Zoloft) withdrawal symptoms typically last up to 1 to 2 weeks, but may last even longer in some people. You should avoid abruptly stopping sertraline treatment unless otherwise directed by your healthcare provider. Gradually reducing the dose over 2 to 4 weeks can help to prevent severe withdrawal symptoms in most people, and should be directed by your doctor.
Q: How long does Zoloft (sertraline) take to work? A: Zoloft (sertraline), a common SSRI antidepressant, can take about 4 to 6 weeks of regular dosing to reach its full therapeutic effect for depression. For other uses, such as obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) or posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a full effect may take up to 12 weeks of treatment. When prescribed for premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), benefits may seen in the first menstrual cycle after starting treatment.
Triplet: ["sertraline", "has withdrawal duration", "may last longer in some people"]

Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

A. 'has duration of treatment': The subject drug is typically taken for the length of time specified by the object entity.
B. 'has withdrawal symptom': When the subject drug is stopped abruptly, the patient may experience the symptom specified by the object entity.
C. 'has overdose symptom': An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
